bandReport.notes: Items 51-75, contiguous, no gaps, no repeats. Item 51 starts whole at the top of p22-c1 and item 75 ends whole at the foot of p30-c2 ('[ P.T.O.'), so neither band edge is cut. All five pages are English. COLUMN CROPS: the automatic split is clean on all five pages; no question text crosses the gutter. Only footer folios ('23', '25', '27', '29', '31') straddle the gutter and appear at the edge of both crops. On p30-c2 a few stray single letters ('s', 'e') sit at the far left edge; they belong to no English item (Hindi show-through / edge artefacts) and were ignored. Faint Hindi show-through from the verso is visible on most crops and was ignored. FIDELITY: the booklet prints decimals with a raised dot (2·5, 1·5, 3·5); recorded as ordinary decimal points (item 58 options, item 70 table). Item 52 and items 54/55 print 'Select the answer using the code given below.' (no 'correct'), transcribed as printed. Item 74 options print '1 and 2' / '1 and 3' without 'only', as printed. Item 70's data grid is a pipe table in the stem (single item, so not context); dashes in the grid are printed em-dash placeholders, kept as '—'. FIGURE: item 68 depends on a diagram of a wall split into 5 rectangles (left two columns each split into a top and bottom cell, plus one full-height cell on the right); its options are numbers. CLASSIFICATION judgement calls: 52 (CEDAW) filed under Current Affairs and IR / United Nations and its Agencies; 53 (Rajya Sabha seat allocation) under Centre-State Relations and Federalism / Schedules (Fourth Schedule); 70 (route counting with times) under Route and Network Puzzles; 73 (islands, some in the news) under Geography.

questions.stem:
Suppose \(1 \le x, y, z \le 9\) are integers such that \(x > z\). Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the three-digit numbers given by \(\alpha = xyz\) and \(\beta = zyx\) so that \(x, y, z\) are the digits as they are shown. Set \(\gamma = \alpha - \beta\). How many of the following statements are always true?
I. 2 does not divide \(\gamma\).
II. 3 divides \(\gamma\).
III. 5 does not divide \(\gamma\).
IV. 7 does not divide \(\gamma\).
V. 11 divides \(\gamma\).
VI. 13 does not divide \(\gamma\).
Select the correct answer.

questions.stem:
P, Q, R and S are four places. To travel from P to R, one travels via Q and to travel from P to S, one travels via both Q and R. Between P and Q, there are 3 routes; between Q and R, there are 4 routes; and between R and S, there are 5 routes. The time taken to travel through these routes is exhibited on the following chart in hours for a specific vehicle :

| Routes | Between P and Q | Between Q and R | Between R and S |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 3 | 1.5 | 2 |
| 3 | 4 | 2 | 2.5 |
| 4 | — | 2 | 3 |
| 5 | — | — | 3.5 |

How many possible routes are there if the journey takes exactly 7 hours?
